      "source": [
        "\"\"\"Example Scenario\n",
        "Imagine we are analyzing student test scores in a class. Scores are normally distributed with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 10.\n",
        "We want to:\n",
        "\n",
        "Plot the probability density curve.\n",
        "\n",
        "Simulate random scores and visualize them.\n",
        "\"\"\"\n",
        "\n",
        "import numpy as np\n",
        "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
        "from scipy.stats import norm\n",
        "\n",
        "# Parameters\n",
        "mu = 70    # mean\n",
        "sigma = 10 # standard deviation\n",
        "\n",
        "# Generate x values (range of scores)\n",
        "x = np.linspace(mu - 4*sigma, mu + 4*sigma, 1000)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Calculate PDF values\n",
        "pdf = norm.pdf(x, mu, sigma)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Generate random sample data\n",
        "np.random.seed(42)\n",
        "sample_scores = np.random.normal(mu, sigma, 1000)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Plot PDF curve\n",
        "plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))\n",
        "plt.plot(x, pdf, label=f'N({mu}, {sigma}²)', color='red', linewidth=2)\n",
        "plt.hist(sample_scores, bins=30, density=True, alpha=0.6, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')\n",
        "plt.title(\"Normal Distribution - Student Scores\")\n",
        "plt.xlabel(\"Score\")\n",
        "plt.ylabel(\"Density\")\n",
        "plt.legend()\n",
        "plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)\n",
        "plt.show()\n"
      ]
    }
  ],
